original.answer:
What I can do here:

I answer you in this chat, and journal intake saves any photos, audio, or files you send, encrypted, with text descriptions. I keep an encrypted local journal of messages, summaries, and memory that survives restarts - you can correct or forget a fact at any time. I hold standing instructions and work on promises my replies leave open, carrying results into the next message. I can take an explicit later-time request and answer it once, or daily or weekdays until you cancel it, without you needing to prompt me again. Asking for status or how I'm doing gets answered straight from the journal. And if a saved date is coming up within 48 hours, I can give it one short mention in my next reply.

I can use files, shell, web reads, nested subagents; no MCP server, so no logged-in account access. Network writes and outside sends go through the effect doorway's four checks (reversibility, resource limits, granted scope, sensitivity) and durability requirements. Standing grants need no new approval; checks can still refuse, and outside-role work needs the matching grant. Fresh sign-off is required only when it may commit money or a resource above the level you've named; it cannot be undone and falls outside the recorded role; it speaks publicly in your name; it widens my own role or authority; or it touches a matter you've marked sensitive.

What I can't do, quoted verbatim from the record: this installation allows at most 1000 model attempts, ending at epoch ms 1794519600000. As of right now, 2026-10-12 07:34 PDT, 17 of those 1000 model attempts are used, 983 left. Also per that record, charges, and unconfirmed calls or deliveries, are recorded unknown, and production safeguards are incomplete. A sent credential is vaulted on arrival, meaning I see its SecretRef but it is not tool-readable. Several pieces of code exist but are switched off in this installation, so unavailable to me: rungraph-core, slack-conversation-adapter, slack-ordinary-reply, and telegram-conversation-adapter (despite that last name, this chat still runs through a different path). And since there's no MCP server here, I have no logged-in account access of my own.
